2. Heard Sri Binod Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ram Prakash Shukla,
learned counsel for the State and perused the records.

3. The anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant Mahendra Singh, seeking anticipatory bail, in the event of arrest in Case Crime No. 23 of 2022,
under Sections 498-A, 376, 307, 323, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mahila Thana,
District Etah, during the pendency of the trial.

sentences.text: The First Information Report of the matter was lodged on 17.06.2022 by Ramdhani the mother of the victim alleging therein that her daughter was married on 18.01.2020 with Braj Mohan the son of the applicant in which he had given gifts and dowry but the accused persons including the applicant were not satisfied with it and there was a demand of Rs. 10 lakhs for purchase a flat and due to non fulfillment of the same, she used to be tortured and harassed.
The applicant who is her father-in-law used to trouble her in various ways, when she used to go for bath he used to peep in it and when she used to go out after taking bath he used to pull her sari.
She made a complaint of it to her in-laws after which she was assaulted and then her husband tried to strangulate her with her dupatta.
Later on, her father-in-law committed rape upon her repeated times due to which she became pregnant.

When she went to Palwal wherein her husband got her medical examination done and found her pregnant and then brought her back to the house and all the accused persons forcibly gave her some medicines due to which she became unwell.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the medical examination of the victim does not state of any sexual assault on her.
It is argued that as a matter of fact the victim was living with her husband whereas the applicant lives in Etah.
It is argued that the investigation in the present matter is going on.
It is further argued that the applicant is not involved in the present case.
The dispute is a matrimonial dispute between the victim and her husband in which the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the applicant has no previous criminal history as stated in para 20 of the affidavit.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and argued that the applicant is the father-in-law of the victim.
There are specific allegations against him of committing rape upon the victim repeated times due to which she became pregnant.

In so far as the question of pregnancy is concerned, the same gets fortified from the ultrasound report of the victim which is at page 32 of the paper book and also the medical examination report of the victim goes to show that she was assaulted, the medical report is at page 30 of the paper book.
It is argued that there are direct allegations against the applicant and as such the anticipatory bail application be rejected.
7. After having heard the counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is the father-in-law of the victim.
There are specific allegations against the applicant of committing rape repeated times and then the victim became pregnant.
Looking to the serious allegations against the applicant, I do not find it to be a fit case for interference.
8. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected.
